newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican ruling party humbled in Morelos state vote.
newsitem.headline: Mexican ruling party humbled in Morelos state vote.

text.p: Mexico's opposition humbled the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in a crucial state vote last week, stripping the PRI of majority control of the state congress, final results showed on Saturday.

Morelos, an important state due to its close proximity just south of Mexico City, was also a key election ahead of the widely watched mid-term elections of July 6, when several governorships will be contested and the control of national congress is at stake.
The PRI can now be outvoted in the local congress of the agricultural state. Adding to the woes of President Ernesto Zedillo's PRI was the fact that the party only held onto 16 of 33 town halls.

The PRI has held almost total power in Mexico for 68 years except for a handful of governorships and local legislatures. Before the vote, which took place last Sunday, the PRI had an absolute majority in the local legislature and held all but one of the Morelos mayoralties.

Mexico's left-leaning Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) grabbed 13 mayoral posts in Morelos and the conservative National Action Party (PAN) took two town halls, including the all-important state capital, Cuernavaca. The PRI kept 17 mayoral jobs and a local party won the remaining one.

In the state congress, the PRI now holds 13 seats but could be easily outvoted by other parties, which combined have 17 seats. The PRD took 11 seats, the PAN five and the Civic Party of the People of Morelos (PCM) one.

The opposition said the importance of the vote was spelled out by the fact it took electoral authorities seven days to determine a final result in state capital Cuernavaca, where 121,705 ballots were cast.
"It is more a reality of the PRI taking seven days to accept defeat than a lack of mathematical capacity on the part of electoral authorities," said one PRD official who declined to be named.
PAN members celebrated the narrow 400-vote victory in Cuernavaca but the more significant strides taken in Morelos were those of the PRD, a party in recent years overshadowed by the PRI and PAN.

PRD election successes have been few and far between, but the gains made in this vote, including mayoral victories in the second and third state cities of Cuautla and Jojutla, augur well for the centre-left party.

Attention will now turn to the upcoming vote for the mayor of Mexico City, where residents will elect their own mayor for the first time on July 6. In the past the president has hand-picked the capital's mayor, whose official title will become governor after the July vote.

Veteran politician Cuauhtemoc Cardenas kicked off his campaign to become Mexico City mayor on Friday. Polls show Cardenas, son of a popular ex-president, as the front runner for arguably the country's second most-powerful post.
